title: A0 rectangular-wall compressional Alfvén benchmark
introduction: Independent cold Hall reference and accepted nonlinear RK4 trajectories in the grid-aligned RZ conductor box. The final evidence includes fixed-box refinement, half-step timing, matched quiet drift and a physical wall-distance control.

notation.meaning: Physical poloidal cross-section coordinates in m
Toroidal harmonic index and retained Fourier cutoff
Toroidal magnetic perturbation parallel to the vacuum guide field

known_issues.label: Independent branch screening and full-domain near-wall limits

pages.title: Cold Hall short control
pages.introduction: A previously defined exact axial standing wave checks the repaired spatial path before the toroidal mode comparison.

figures.title: Axial wave phase and span error
figures.caption: The 12 ns accepted trajectory is compared to the independently given wave at each saved time.

pages.title: Tracked n_phi=1 mode
pages.introduction: The modal phase is fitted from accepted state outputs. The independent reference and the local frozen source are recorded separately.

figures.title: 16×16 accepted frequency and phase
figures.caption: Fitted frequency 5.648532 MHz and independent value 6.176967 MHz.

figures.title: Parallel magnetic field structure
figures.caption: Full-box overlap 0.764 and overlap 0.952 at ≥0.20 m from the wall. Separate RMS normalization makes the comparison a shape diagnostic.

figures.title: Magnetic polarization
figures.caption: The magnetic components use the same phase and one parallel-field normalization. Colorbars are separate by component.

pages.title: Absolute physical fields and matched differences
pages.introduction: The first two columns show the full field in the quiet and perturbed runs at the same physical time. The right column uses the difference at that time.

figures.title: 16×16 physical RZ sections
figures.caption: Ion density, magnetic magnitude, ion speed and electric magnitude at φ=0. The full density color scale starts at zero. Black lines denote the conducting walls.

figures.title: 16×16 pressures before and after subtraction
figures.caption: The scalar ion pressure and both electron pressure components are shown in physical units.

figures.title: Wider-box 20×20 physical RZ sections
figures.caption: The left column uses the static equilibrium. The middle column is the accepted total field at 748.8 ns. Black lines mark the wider conducting walls.

figures.title: Narrow-box 12×12 physical RZ sections
figures.caption: The static equilibrium and accepted total fields use a common scale. The right column subtracts the static equilibrium.

pages.title: Separate mesh, time-step and wall controls
pages.introduction: The mesh series holds the physical walls fixed. The wall series holds the cell spacing and the time step fixed.

figures.title: Separate physical and numerical sensitivities
figures.caption: Fixed-domain grid refinement, matched half-step phase gap and same-spacing physical wall movement.

figures.title: Wider physical wall structure
figures.caption: The wider box uses the same 0.075 m cells as the narrow 16×16 case.

figures.title: Physical structures across the three meshes
figures.caption: Fixed-box grids are shown beside the wider physical box. Dotted lines identify the fixed 0.20 m wall collar, and all panels share one normalized scale.

pages.title: Physical spatial resolution
pages.introduction: The continuous reference supplies the directional wavelengths and dominant lobe widths. The fixed-box grid and time estimates are kept separate from the wider physical box.

figures.title: Independent mode scales and cuts
figures.caption: The cuts mark the connected amplitude half-maximum intervals in R and Z. Grid counts and the next fixed-box measurement are recorded in the methods.

conclusions: A0 follows the independently identified compressional branch over four measured periods and resolves the dominant interior structure. The full-box near-wall shape and absolute frequency retain measurable discrepancies at this resolution.
